title: The Yes Bank – Rana Kapoor Fraud
dek: A private bank's co-founder allegedly approved a ₹3,700 crore investment in a struggling lender's debentures in exchange for a ₹600 crore kickback routed to his family's company — days before that same lender's own fraud became public.

heroStat.label: alleged kickback routed to a company owned by Rana Kapoor's daughters

promise.quote: Yes Bank's investment decisions, including its debenture purchases, will be made on commercial merit and free of personal financial benefit to the bank's decision-makers.
promise.madeBy: Yes Bank, under co-founder and then-CEO Rana Kapoor
promise.context: The CBI alleges Yes Bank invested ₹3,700 crore in short-term debentures issued by DHFL, and that DHFL's promoters, the Wadhawan brothers, paid a ₹600 crore kickback to the Kapoor family in the form of a loan to DoIT Urban Ventures, a company owned by Kapoor's daughters.

target.description: Investment decisions made on commercial merit through the bank's normal approval process, with no undisclosed personal financial benefit to any decision-maker or their family.
target.standard: RBI norms on related-party transactions and conflict-of-interest disclosure for bank executives.

reality.description: The CBI arrested Rana Kapoor on 8 March 2020 and registered a case against him, DHFL, and DoIT Urban Ventures. The Enforcement Directorate separately attached roughly ₹2,203 crore in assets belonging to Kapoor and others. In April 2020, the CBI also booked Kapoor's wife and three daughters. DHFL's Kapil and Dheeraj Wadhawan were separately arrested in the same case.

gap.note: Both figures come from the CBI's stated allegations as reported in the press; neither has yet been confirmed by a court finding.
